thread:
incident-bot: Pager alert: 3xx/5xx surge and conn resets observed for inference-api in eu-central-2 (high error rate). Automated routing fallback tripped. Severity: P1. PagerDuty: paging on-call.

sarah: seeing ~20% 5xx across /v1/generate, spikes started ~3m ago. Grafana: 502/504 + TLS conn resets. Errors concentrated on nodepool-euc2-ingress.

alex: confirmed. sample from load tests: curl returns 502 with body 'upstream reset by peer'.

mike: logs from envoy show repeated RST_STREAM and upstream connection failure to target group tg-euc2-models. Copying a snippet:

```
[2026-03-15T09:12:45Z] envoy info: upstream reset: connection reset by peer, host=tg-euc2-models/i-0a1b2c3d4e
[2026-03-15T09:12:46Z] envoy warning: accept queue full, connection dropped
```

linh: Route53 weighted routing shows euc2 weight didn't respond to healthcheck flip; there's a drift where traffic still hitting euc2 despite fallback policy. I'm seeing a ~15s delay on DNS weight propagation in our internal controller.

sarah: customer-impact: embedding and generation customers in EU are seeing timeouts and 5xx. Top customers: ledgerly-prod and searchly-prod showing high error budgets. Raising DRI to James for customer comms.

james: on it. Will prep status blast once we have mitigation. Any immediate mitigations? can we shift traffic?

alex: we can manually set route53 weights for the eu routing record to 0 for eu-central-2 to force cross-region failover to eu-west-1. Doing a dry-run in console now.

mike: also seeing NLB target health flaps for backend instances behind tg-euc2-models; health checks failing with TLS handshake timeouts. Possibly connection tracking or kernel level issue on instances.

sarah: ops-bot, can you show current target group health and NLB metrics?

ops-bot: Current summary: tg-euc2-models: 3/8 healthy. Increased unhealthy count over last 4m. NLB connections in flight spiked x3. Average backend latency increased from 50ms -> 900ms before resets.

linh: kube-ops: some nodes in asg-euc2-models reported restart of docker daemon around the time of spike (03:09Z). Could be rolling restart or platform agent causing connection teardown.

alex: immediate plan: 1) set Route53 weight for eu-central-2 -> 0, 2) scale up envoy/ingress in euc2 to relieve accept queue, 3) cordon + drain clearly unhealthy model instances to stop flapping targets, 4) open mitigation ticket with infra.

mike: I'm running the commands now. kubectl scale deploy envoy-ingress -n infra --replicas=8

sarah: manual Route53 change in progress (updating weighted record - using our internal console to avoid propagation delays). I'll post once applied.

incident-bot: Route53 change initiated by sarah at 2026-03-15T09:15:12Z. Weight eu-central-2 -> 0. Fallback region eu-west-1 weight -> 100.

alex: curl to the canonical host now returns 200 from eu-west-1. Sample:

```
$ curl -s -D - https://inference-api.prod.internal/v1/health -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{remote_ip}"
200 18.194.23.11
```

mike: envoy pods scaled to 8. Observed accept queue drop rate reduced ~80% after scaling. Still seeing some backend unhealthy targets — starting cordon/drain of the worst ones: i-0a1b2c3d4e & i-0f9e8d7c6b.

linh: draining nodes. Marking as out of service in target group.

sarah: James, can you draft a short status update: region eu-central-2 experiencing degraded ingress due to backend instance network flaps; traffic shifted to eu-west-1; mitigations in progress. Customers may see elevated latency and occasional errors during failover.

james: posting now. Will include link to postmortem stub. tagging affected customers for transparency.

mike: infra team reachable. Opening ticket INC-5832 with EC2 team for kernel/network investigation. Early suspicion: NIC firmware causing sporadic TLS handshake failures under load.

alex: adding temporary policy: reduce keepalive timeouts on NLB -> to avoid stuck connections causing conntrack exhaustion. Command:

```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:...:tg-euc2-models --attributes Key=slow-start.duration-seconds,Value=30
```

sarah: are we seeing any cross-region billing or capacity issues by failing over to eu-west-1? ops-bot, check capacity headroom.

ops-bot: eu-west-1 model pools have ~30% spare capacity. No immediate risk. Cost impact minimal for short-term failover.

linh: monitoring post-change. DNS skew looks resolved; traffic for host influx shows >95% now to eu-west-1. Error rates dropped to baseline for most endpoints.

incident-bot: Pager resolved by sarah at 2026-03-15T09:20:40Z. Incident auto-close pending manual verification. Please keep thread updated with infra RCA and customer impact numbers.

sarah: leaving follow-ups: 1) infra RCA on NIC/daemon restart, 2) fix controller propagation race for Route53 weights, 3) add automation to detect targetgroup health drift and auto-shift earlier, 4) postmortem + customer comms.

james: will coordinate postmortem and email to affected customers. Assigning follow-ups in ticket tracker.

mike: temporary mitigations reverted? I left envoy scaled; plan to scale down to baseline in 30m if stable. Removing manual Route53 override scheduled after 1h once infra RCA done.

linh: adding alert rule to fire if targetgroup healthy < 50% for > 2m to avoid slow detection next time.

sarah: thanks all. If anything regresses ping this thread. I'll add logs and traces to INC-5832.

incident-bot: Note: automated incident timeline saved to /incidents/3764500123/timeline.log (internal).
